title: Ausangate Glaciers Tour Full Day
short_description: Contemplate the majestic glaciers and imposing masses of ice descending from the sacred Apu Ausangate on an unforgettable high-mountain expedition.
long_description:
The Ausangate Glaciers Tour Full Day is one of the most impressive experiences for lovers of nature and high-mountain landscapes in Cusco. This excursion allows you to get up close to the majestic glaciers that form part of Mount Ausangate, the highest peak in the Cusco region and considered one of the most sacred mountains in Andean cosmology.

During the journey, you will pass through small traditional villages, vast high-Andean plains, and landscapes dominated by glacial lakes, peatlands, and herds of alpacas and llamas, until reaching the impressive glaciers descending from Ausangate's snow-capped peaks.

Unlike other adventure routes, this tour offers the opportunity to contemplate massive natural ice formations, observe the process of glacier formation, and enjoy a virtually untouched environment surrounded by mountains soaring above 6,000 meters above sea level. It is an ideal experience for travelers wishing to discover one of the most spectacular landscapes in the Peruvian Andes.
price_note: Includes tourist transport, buffet breakfast and lunch in Cusipata, official bilingual guide, entrance tickets, trekking poles, and emergency oxygen equipment.

days.title: Day 1: Cusco – Cusipata – Ausangate Glaciers – Ausangate Lake – Cusco
days.text:
We will pick you up from your accommodation between 04:00 and 05:00 a.m. to begin our journey toward the town of Cusipata, a drive of approximately 2 hours.

Upon arrival in Cusipata, we will enjoy an Andean buffet breakfast prepared with local ingredients to give us the energy needed for this adventure. After breakfast, we will continue in our transport to the nearest point to the start of the hike.

From there, we will begin a moderately challenging ascent lasting approximately 1 hour until we reach the snow-capped mountain. Along the trail, we will appreciate Ausangate Lake along with other impressive glaciers framing the landscape, offering ideal settings for reflection and photography.

After enjoying the visit, we will hike back along the same path to the starting point, where our transport will be waiting to take us back to Cusipata. Once in Cusipata, we will enjoy a delicious and nutritious lunch. Afterward, we will start the return journey to Cusco, concluding this tour.

faq.pregunta: Is this tour suitable for beginners?
faq.respuesta: Yes, provided the traveler has a reasonable physical condition and has properly acclimatized to Cusco's high altitude.

faq.pregunta: Is it possible to see glaciers all year round?
faq.respuesta: Yes. The Ausangate glaciers maintain permanent snow year-round, although their volume or visual appearance may vary slightly depending on the season.

faq.pregunta: When is the best time to do this tour?
faq.respuesta: Between April and October, during the dry season, which offers the best weather and visibility conditions.

faq.pregunta: Can I rent a horse during the trek?
faq.respuesta: Yes, local community members offer horse rental services at the trail's starting point. The approximate cost ranges between 70 and 80 Soles.
They are not mandatory, but highly recommended to provide better stability. Furthermore, we include trekking poles in our service.

faq.pregunta: What wildlife can be spotted on the trip?
faq.respuesta: Along the route, it is very common to spot alpacas, llamas, vicuñas, high-Andean birds, and various species adapted to mountain ecosystems.

faq.pregunta: Does it get very cold during the tour?
faq.respuesta: Yes, especially in the early morning hours and in areas close to the glaciers. We recommend dressing in thermal layers with a windproof jacket.

faq.pregunta: Are restrooms available along the route?
faq.respuesta: Basic restroom facilities are available at the point where the hike begins and ends.

faq.pregunta: Does this tour operate during the rainy season?
faq.respuesta: Yes, the excursion operates year-round, adjusting the walking pace according to daily weather conditions.
